pool.text:
The box plot below shows the distribution of scores for a class of 30 students on a recent test. The interquartile range (IQR) is 22 marks. The median score is 75 marks. The minimum score is 30 marks, and the maximum score is 98 marks.

Let the first quartile be denoted by \( Q_1 \) and the third quartile be denoted by \( Q_3 \).

If the upper whisker extends to 98 marks, and the third quartile \( Q_3 \) is 86 marks, find the value of \( Q_1 \).
pool.educational_aim: Apply properties and theorems of Statistics & Probability in multi-step exam problems, including finding unknown parameters, interpreting exact diagrams/graphs, and avoiding common algebraic traps.
pool.exam_archetype: Statistics & Probability — Multi-Step Application & Parameter Solve
pool.sol: The interquartile range (IQR) is defined as the difference between the third quartile (\( Q_3 \)) and the first quartile (\( Q_1 \)), i.e., \( \text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 \). We are given that the IQR is 22 marks. We are also given that the third quartile \( Q_3 = 86 \) marks. Substituting these values into the formula, we get: \( 22 = 86 - Q_1 \) To find \( Q_1 \), we rearrange the equation: \( Q_1 = 86 - 22 \) \( Q_1 = 64 \) Therefore, the first quartile is 64 marks. Common errors might include misinterpreting the median as \( Q_1 \) or \( Q_3 \), or incorrectly using the minimum or maximum values in the IQR calculation. [M1] [A1]
hints: The interquartile range (IQR) is defined as the difference between the third quartile (\( Q_3 \)) and the first quartile (\( Q_1 \)), i.e., \( \text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 \).

We are given that the IQR is 22 marks. We are also given that the third quartile \( Q_3 = 86 \) marks. Substituting these values into the formula, we get: \( 22 = 86 - Q_1 \) To find \( Q_1 \), we rearrange the equation: \( Q_1 = 86 - 22 \) \( Q_1 = 64 \).

pool.text:
The box plot below shows the distribution of scores for a class on a recent statistics quiz. The five-number summary is given by minimum, first quartile (Q1), median, third quartile (Q3), and maximum.

If the interquartile range (IQR) is 25, and the median score is 70, find the value of Q1.

pool.sol: The interquartile range (IQR) is defined as the difference between the third quartile (Q3) and the first quartile (Q1), i.e., \( \text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 \). We are given that the IQR is 25. The median of the dataset is given as 70. In a box plot, the median is represented by the line inside the box. Therefore, \( Q_2 = 70 \). The box plot also indicates that the third quartile (Q3) is 70. This is because the right edge of the box aligns with the median line, indicating \( Q_3 = 70 \). Now we can use the IQR formula to find Q1: \( 25 = 70 - Q_1 \) Rearranging the equation to solve for \( Q_1 \): \( Q_1 = 70 - 25 \) \( Q_1 = 45 \) Therefore, the value of Q1 is 45. [M1] [A1]

pool.text:
The masses \(X\) (in grams) of organic coffee packs produced by a roastery are normally distributed with mean \(\mu = 400\text{ g}\) and standard deviation \(\sigma = 20\text{ g}\).
(a) Find the probability that a randomly selected pack has a mass greater than \(425\text{ g}\). [2]
(b) Find the mass \(m\) exceeded by \(10\%\) of the coffee packs. [3]
(c) Given that a pack weighs more than \(400\text{ g}\), find the conditional probability that it weighs more than \(425\text{ g}\). [4]
(d) A quality inspector selects a random box of \(10\) packs. Find the probability that at least \(2\) packs in the box have a mass greater than \(425\text{ g}\). [5]
pool.sol:
IB Markscheme (14 marks — AA/AI SL Paper 2, Section B Extended-Response):
(a) Using GDC normcdf(425, 1E99, 400, 20): \(P(X > 425) = 0.1056\) (or \(0.106\)) [M1] [A1]
(b) \(P(X > m) = 0.10 \implies P(X < m) = 0.90\) [M1]; via invNorm(0.90, 400, 20): \(m = 425.6\text{ g}\) (3 s.f.) [M1] [A1]
(c) Conditional probability \(P(X > 425 \mid X > 400) = \frac{P(X > 425)}{P(X > 400)}\) [M1] [A1] \(= \frac{0.10565}{0.5} = 0.2113\) [M1] [A1]
(d) Let \(Y \sim \text{B}(10, 0.10565)\) [M1] [A1]
\(P(Y \ge 2) = 1 - P(Y \le 1)\) [M1] \(= 1 - 0.71415 = 0.2858\) (or \(0.286\)) [M1] [A1]
hints: IB Markscheme (14 marks — AA/AI SL Paper 2, Section B Extended-Response): (a) Using GDC normcdf(425, 1E99, 400, 20): \(P(X > 425) = 0.1056\) (or \(0.106\)).
Use the resulting form to finish: \(P(Y \ge 2) = 1 - P(Y \le 1)\) \(= 1 - 0.71415\) (or \(0.286\)).

figure.label: X > 425

pool.text: How many different 4-digit codes can be formed using the digits 1-9 without repetition, if the code must be even?

pool.sol: The last digit must be 2, 4, 6, or 8 (4 choices). The remaining 3 positions are filled from the remaining 8 digits, in order: \( 8\times7\times6=336. \) Total: \( 4\times336=1344. \) [M1] [A1]
hints: The last digit must be 2, 4, 6, or 8 (4 choices).
The remaining 3 positions are filled from the remaining 8 digits, in order: \( 8\times7\times6=336. \) Total.
